name: Celiac disease and gluten sensitivity
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> Celiac disease or gluten sensitivity. Check question: Has a doctor diagnosed celiac disease (blood test or biopsy), wheat allergy, or non-celiac gluten sensitivity, or do you avoid gluten because wheat upsets you? Yes, celiac diagnosed / Yes, gluten or wheat sensitivity diagnosed / I avoid gluten but was never tested / No. Safety question: Are you thinking of starting a gluten-free diet before testing, or is this for a child under 18? (Yes: no targets set; see a doctor first and keep eating gluten until tests are done)

targets.source: ICMR-NIN 2020 (secondary, unverified); no celiac-specific change found. Weight regain after diagnosis may need a doctor/dietitian plan
WHO 2023; DGI 2024. Gluten-free packaged foods often carry more fat (label surveys, secondary)
No ICMR total found; DGI 2024 cereal cap applies (secondary, unverified). Swap gluten grains for gluten-free grains, not for refined starch
FitPlate app-wide cap (WHO 2015 5% of energy, conditional); gluten-free biscuits, cakes and mixes can be high (est.)
About 30 g per 2,000 kcal (as P4/P18); FitPlate keeps the same total and flags it as at risk on a gluten-free diet; sources: ragi, jowar, bajra, maize, pulses, vegetables, fruit (IFCT 2017)
ICMR-NIN 2020 (secondary, unverified); topic 15; 1,200 mg at 60+ and after menopause; priority for bone (P20); ragi is the top gluten-free source (IFCT 2017)
ICMR-NIN 2020 (secondary, unverified) (women 29); topic 21; doctor tests ferritin and sets any iron tablet (P11)
ICMR-NIN 2020 (secondary, unverified); topic 2; lab-guided dose is a doctor decision (P12)
ICMR-NIN 2020 (secondary, unverified); topic 13; doctor checks level (P12)
ICMR-NIN 2020 (secondary, unverified) (women 220); topic 12; gluten-free flours are rarely fortified
Topic 30 (women 2,000 ml); no celiac-specific fluid value found. Follow your doctor's advice.

bloodMarkers.marker: tTG-IgA (tissue transglutaminase IgA antibody) with total IgA
bloodMarkers.target: Diagnostic test only valid while eating gluten; positive cut-off is lab-specific (Not found as one number); the doctor interprets. After diagnosis the doctor may repeat it to check diet adherence; no FitPlate target
bloodMarkers.source: ACG 2023 via AAFP and JAMA summaries (secondary); ICMR celiac guideline (not opened)

bloodMarkers.target: Doctor-led confirmation; the app stores no value
bloodMarkers.source: ACG 2023 via MDCalc summary; IAPM-ISG 2021 biopsy consensus (via search)

bloodMarkers.target: WHO anaemia cut-offs 13.0 (men) and 12.0 g/dL (women) as in P11; doctor decides
Stored only; doctor-interpreted; see P12, topics 12 and 13
Doctor-led; adults at diagnosis may be scanned; see P20
bloodMarkers.source: NICE NG20 surveillance discussion (via search; exact wording not confirmed); P20

bloodMarkers.marker: Calcium, magnesium, zinc, ALT, TSH, blood sugar
bloodMarkers.target: Stored only; no FitPlate comment. Celiac disease is linked with raised liver enzymes and thyroid and type 1 diabetes autoimmunity (general; Not sourced here)

waterMl.notes: No change from the general FitPlate range (topic 30: 2,500 ml men, 2,000 ml women as drinks, est.). Celiac disease alone does not change the target. During diarrhoea keep drinking as usual and see a doctor if it lasts more than a few days, or if there is blood, fever or dizziness. With kidney, heart or liver disease, pregnancy, a fluid limit or a diuretic show the general range only. Follow your doctor's advice.

foodsFavour: rice, idli, dosa, poha (check), khichdi, steamed rice dishes
ragi, jowar, bajra, maize (makka), rajgira (amaranth), kuttu (buckwheat), quinoa, sabudana in measured portions
dals, rajma, chole, chana, moong, sprouts and besan from a gluten-free source
vegetables, fruit, curd, chaas, paneer, eggs, fish, chicken cooked at home
ragi and sesame for calcium; methi, drumstick and amaranth leaves; nuts and seeds (topics 15, 21)
packaged foods only with a gluten-free label (FSSAI: below 20 mg/kg) or an ingredient list checked every time
pure or certified gluten-free oats only after the doctor/dietitian agrees
foodsLimit: wheat, atta, maida, suji/rava, dalia, sevai/semiya, barley (jau), rye and all their products (roti, paratha, naan, puri, bread, pav, biscuits, noodles, pasta)
regular oats and 'multigrain' atta or sattu blends (barley or wheat may be inside)
soy sauce, malt, malt vinegar, beer, sauces and ketchup, stock cubes, instant soups, masala blends and compounded hing unless the label says gluten-free
papad, namkeen, fried foods cooked in shared oil, street food from shared tawas
refined gluten-free biscuits, cakes and breads as daily foods (more sugar and fat, less protein and fibre in label surveys; secondary)
'gluten-free' claims on loose flour from a shared chakki

cautionDishes.reason: Flour in batter in many kitchens (est.)
Regular oats are often cross-contaminated; only certified gluten-free oats, if the doctor agrees
Dum biryani is sometimes sealed with wheat dough; ask
Hing and shared frying oil; some batters add rava (est.)
Hing and masala check; besan source
Bread crumbs or maida binder in many recipes (est.)

conflictsWith.rule: Untreated celiac disease can cause secondary lactose intolerance that often fades as the gut heals; lactose limits may be temporary; changes are doctor/dietitian-led (P18)
IBS is diagnosed only after celiac testing; do not drop wheat before tests; one change at a time with a diary (P16)
Celiac disease is a cause of iron-deficiency anaemia; iron target raised in priority; ferritin and any tablet are doctor-led (P11, topic 21)
Malabsorption can lower vitamin D, B12 and folate; levels and doses are doctor-led (P12)
Bone loss can accompany celiac disease; calcium 1,000-1,200 mg and DEXA are doctor-led (P20)
Gluten-free breads, biscuits and rice-based swaps can raise glycaemic load; the diabetes carbohydrate and fibre rules (P1) apply on top of gluten-free rules
Vegan plus gluten-free narrows protein and B12 sources; use pulses, soy, quinoa and fortified foods; B12 is doctor-checked (P34)
Jain plus gluten-free: hing is common in Jain cooking, so use gluten-free hing; iron and B12 gaps as P33 (P33)

warnings: Do not start a gluten-free diet before blood tests and, if advised, a biopsy; stopping gluten first can give a false-negative result
Celiac disease can only be diagnosed by a doctor; FitPlate does not diagnose
Once diagnosed, the diet is strict and lifelong; even small amounts of gluten matter, so check labels, shared utensils, chakki-milled flour and eating out
Millets, besan and sattu are not automatically safe: cross-contamination at mills, 'multigrain' blends and barley sattu contain gluten
Children under 18, pregnancy and breastfeeding: doctor and dietitian first
Blood in stool, weight loss, severe diarrhoea, anaemia, blistering itchy rash, fractures or poor growth in a child: talk to a doctor
The app never suggests supplement doses; iron, calcium, vitamin D, B12 and folate tablets are doctor-led
